findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor roster file uploaded via aws_s3_bucket_object.reports_seed_object) are stored unencrypted at rest by default.
This bucket stores financial ledger export data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial records unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest despite versioning and logging being configured.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbook content (which may include internal procedures or sensitive configuration details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid AWS canned ACL (the correct value would be "log-delivery-write"). A malformed or unintended ACL string on a bucket intended to receive access logs risks either deployment failure or, if resolved unexpectedly by a provider default, granting broader access than intended to a sensitive audit trail bucket.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket holding sensitive financial ledger data, so there is no explicit safeguard preventing future bucket policy or ACL changes from exposing it publicly.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured for the audit trail bucket, leaving it without a defense-in-depth control against accidental public exposure of audit logs.
